Aiya, let me think this through. Three mu of cotton — same as last year, same as the year before. I'll talk through it the way I would with my neighbor over tea.

---

I'm seventy-five now and these three mu of cotton are all I have to look after. My husband passed some years back and the children are working in the city — they send a little money but the land is mine to manage. I've grown cotton on this ground since I was a girl, so I know what this soil does. Around our village most of us still do cotton because the wheat-maize rotation has too much running back and forth for one person to handle, and cotton you can stretch out over the season at a slower pace.

The biggest thing on my mind is labor. I can't bend down picking for eight hours like I used to — my back won't take it. So I plan from the start to hire two or three women from the village for the fall picking. That's my biggest cost after fertilizer, and the village rate keeps climbing each year, but there's no way around it. For spring tillage I pay the man with the small tractor — he does all the small plots in our lane in a day. I lay the plastic film myself with my neighbor helping; we trade work back and forth, no money changes hands.

For seed I buy the Bt cotton from the agricultural supply shop in town — the kind with the built-in protection against bollworm. Costs more than saving my own seed, but before this variety came in the bollworm used to ruin everything. About 60 yuan of seed per mu. For fertilizer I put down one bag of compound (the 15-15-15) before planting, then top-dress urea twice — once when the buds are forming in early summer, once when the bolls are setting. Comes out to about 13 kg of nitrogen per mu, which is what the extension fellow told us years back and what I've stuck with. I'd put on a bit more if urea were cheaper, but the price has been high two years running so I hold to what I know.

Water I get from the village well — pumping costs electricity money, so I don't waste it. I'll irrigate once after planting if the spring is dry, to get even emergence, and once more at flowering if there's been no rain. Two times in a normal year. For pests, beyond the Bt I spray a herbicide right after planting under the film, and I watch for aphids and spider mites in summer — if I see them I spray, if not I save the money. Before picking I'll spray a defoliant so the leaves drop and the women can work faster. At my age that little step is worth every yuan.

If the year is normal I expect about 250 kg of lint per mu — roughly 700 kg of seed cotton before ginning. Last year was alright. I don't push for big yields anymore; I just want a decent crop with no surprises.
